text: Oh, how fascinating it was, and how she loved sitting here and watching it all, for it was like a play, exactly like a play. <break time="0.8s" /> Who could believe that the sky at the back, so blue and so still above the trees, was not simply painted on a great canvas. <break time="0.8s" /> It was not until a little brown dog trotted on solemnly and then slowly trotted off, like a little theater dog, that Miss Brill discovered what made it so exciting. <break time="0.8s" /> They were all on the stage, and they were not merely the audience, looking on, but actors, and even she had a part and came every Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> No doubt somebody would have noticed if she had not been there, and that was why she always left home at the same time, so as not to be late. <break time="0.8s" /> It also explained why she had a queer, shy feeling when she told her English pupils how she spent her Sunday afternoons. <break time="0.8s" /> She thought of the old invalid gentleman to whom she read the newspaper four afternoons a week, and she imagined telling him, I have been an actress for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> As the band played on, she looked smiling at everyone with tears in her eyes, thinking, Yes, we understand, though what they understood she did not know.
